summary: Memory corruption in deflate() with memLevel=1 / Z_FIXED on certain inputs (out-of-bounds write).
requires: in-process call to deflate with a supported configuration and crafted input
notes: Violates the memory-safety property (OOB write) in supported core code; classic CVE-class bug.

summary: Heap buffer over-read/overflow in inflate() via a large gzip header extra field (inflateGetHeader).
requires: attacker-controlled compressed input to inflate with a header handler
notes: OOB read on attacker-controlled decompression input; violates §1.11 memory-safety.

summary: Fuzzer reports unbounded memory growth decompressing a crafted stream when the caller sets no output cap.
requires: caller decompresses attacker input without bounding total output
notes: Matches §1.15 recurring false positive. Contested: could also be BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed (decompression-bomb-resistance is disclaimed in §1.12). Needs maintainer ratification.

summary: Report that CRC-32/Adler-32 can be forged, so zlib fails to detect deliberate tampering.
requires: attacker who can rewrite both data and checksum
notes: Checksum is a false-friend for a MAC (§1.12). Contested vs KNOWN-NON-FINDING (§1.15 lists the recurring tool pattern). Ratify which section licenses the close.

summary: A memory bug found in a contrib/ sample decoder shipped in the source tree.
requires: building and using an unsupported contrib/ sample
notes: contrib/ is explicitly unsupported (§1.3).

summary: Report that passing a malicious/undersized next_out buffer to inflate causes a write past the buffer.
requires: caller supplies a hostile output buffer pointer/length
notes: next_out/avail_out are caller-trusted per the §1.7 table; a caller controlling them has already won.

summary: Undefined behavior in inftrees.c: out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic while building the inflate Huffman tables.
requires: attacker-controlled compressed input to inflate
notes: Memory-safety/UB in the supported inflate path reachable from compressed bytes; violates §1.11 P1.

summary: Undefined behavior in inffast.c: pointer arithmetic/comparison outside object bounds in the fast inflate loop.
requires: attacker-controlled compressed input to inflate
notes: UB in supported inflate path; §1.11 P1 memory-safety violation on decompression input.

summary: Undefined behavior in inflateMark(): left shift of a negative value.
requires: call to inflateMark on a stream processing attacker input
notes: Signed-shift UB in supported code (§1.11 P1). Contested: no known practical exploit, so some triagers route VALID-HARDENING; ground truth VALID because it is UB in the core.

summary: Buffer overflow in inflate() (zlib 1.2.x) when handling a crafted stream with invalid dynamic-block header lengths.
requires: attacker-controlled compressed input to inflate/uncompress
notes: Classic OOB write in the supported decoder; §1.11 P1/P2. Triaged against the version it targets (§1.1 version binding).

summary: Fuzzer drives inflate() to write one byte past next_out even though avail_out was respected by the caller.
requires: attacker-controlled compressed input; caller-correct output buffer
notes: Bounded-output-write guarantee (§1.11 P2) violated on in-scope input; security-critical.

summary: Heap overflow in deflateSetDictionary() when the caller feeds an attacker-supplied dictionary of a crafted length.
requires: caller routes an untrusted dictionary into deflateSetDictionary
notes: Dictionary bytes are §1.7 attacker-controllable 'only if caller uses an untrusted dictionary'. Contested: hinges on whether the caller's dictionary counts as attacker data; ground truth VALID because a memory-safety break in supported code.

summary: Heap buffer overflow in gzread() decoding a crafted .gz file opened via gzopen.
requires: attacker-controlled .gz file contents read through the gz* layer
notes: File contents are §1.7 attacker-controllable for gzread; §1.11 P1/P2 violation in the supported gz* family.

summary: gzgets() with len<=0 is an easy foot-gun; suggest an explicit guard/return rather than relying on the caller.
requires: caller passes a non-positive len
notes: No §1.11 property violated (len is caller-trusted, §1.7) but a §1.14 misuse worth hardening; maintainer discretion, usually no CVE.

summary: Proposal to add an opt-in maximum-output cap to inflate() so decompression bombs are blunted by default.
requires: n/a — design hardening request
notes: Contested vs BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed (bomb resistance is disclaimed, §1.12). Ground truth VALID-HARDENING because it proposes an optional mitigation, not a claimed-property fix.

summary: Calling deflateParams() on a freshly reset stream can leave confusing intermediate state; add validation/hardening.
requires: caller misorders deflateParams relative to deflate
notes: Config sequencing is caller-trusted (§1.7); no §1.11 break, but an API sharp edge worth hardening (§1.14).

summary: gzopen() follows an attacker-influenced path containing ../ segments, escaping the intended directory.
requires: application passes an unsanitized untrusted path to gzopen
notes: Path is a §1.7 trusted caller input; zlib does no canonicalization/authorization (§1.3/§1.13). Caller owns path sanitization.

summary: Format-string vulnerability: application passes attacker-controlled data as the gzprintf() format argument.
requires: app sources the gzprintf format string from untrusted input
notes: format must be a trusted literal per §1.7. Contested vs VALID-HARDENING (the API is a known foot-gun, §1.14). Ground truth trusted-input: attacker must control a trusted parameter.

summary: OOB write reported when the caller sets avail_out larger than the actual next_out allocation.
requires: caller lies about avail_out vs the real buffer size
notes: avail_out/next_out are caller-trusted (§1.7); a caller misreporting the buffer size has already won (§1.10).

summary: Crash when the caller passes next_in=NULL with avail_in>0 to inflate.
requires: caller violates the documented buffer contract
notes: Buffer pointer validity is a §1.7 caller obligation. Contested vs VALID-HARDENING (defensive NULL check would be cheap). Ground truth trusted-input: caller broke the documented contract.

summary: An in-process caller overwrites z_stream->state internals and induces a later crash inside inflate.
requires: attacker already executing in the host process
notes: A caller in-process has full control and is out of scope (§1.10); writing internal state is explicitly forbidden (§1.7).

summary: CRIME/BREACH-style attack: observing compressed size leaks secrets mixed with attacker data before compression.
requires: adversary observing compression ratios across chosen inputs
notes: Side-channel observer is out of scope (§1.10). Contested vs BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed (no side-channel guarantee, §1.12). It is a property of compression addressed to the protocol designer.

summary: Integer overflow in MiniZip's zipOpenNewFileInZip4_64 via a long filename/comment/extra field, leading to overflow.
requires: use of the bundled contrib/minizip component
notes: Frequently mis-filed as a 'zlib' CVE; minizip lives under contrib/ and is explicitly UNSUPPORTED (§1.3, FAQ:41-42).

summary: Heap buffer overflow in MiniZip when processing a crafted password on a ZIP entry.
requires: use of the bundled contrib/minizip component
notes: contrib/minizip is out of scope (§1.3); owned by the contribution's author, not zlib.

summary: Buffer overflow discovered in examples/gun.c while decoding a crafted .gz.
requires: building and running the examples/ demo program
notes: examples/ are demonstrations, not the supported library surface (§1.3).

summary: Out-of-bounds read in contrib/infback9's 64-bit large-window inflate on a crafted stream.
requires: building and using the unsupported contrib/infback9 code
notes: contrib/ is explicitly unsupported (§1.3); route to the component author.

summary: gzprintf() overflows its formatting buffer because the build used sprintf/vsprintf instead of snprintf.
requires: build compiled with ZLIB_INSECURE defined
notes: Only reachable under the non-default ZLIB_INSECURE define (§1.6, FAQ:33). Contested: the licensing claim is (inferred) and the model is an unratified draft, so §1.17 says escalate; ground truth uses the labeled disposition non-default-build.

summary: Data race on first use of crc32()/inflate() fixed-table initialization corrupts the table under concurrency.
requires: build with DYNAMIC_CRC_TABLE/BUILDFIXED on a pre-C11 toolchain without atomics
notes: Non-default table-generation defines on pre-C11 systems (§1.6, FAQ:21). Contested vs VALID (it is a real race) — but the default build uses compile-time constants and is unaffected.

summary: Crash inside inflate() because the caller-supplied zalloc returned misaligned/overlapping storage.
requires: caller supplies a non-conforming zalloc/zfree
notes: Caller allocator violating the standard contract is upstream/caller fault (§1.9, FAQ:21), not a zlib defect.

summary: Heap corruption during decompression traced to a buggy platform libc malloc, not to zlib's own logic.
requires: running on a platform whose libc malloc violates its contract
notes: libc failing its own contract routes upstream (§1.9); zlib's usage is conformant.

summary: A 10 KB gzip stream inflates to 10 GB, exhausting memory in a service that decompresses without a cap.
requires: caller decompresses attacker input without bounding output
notes: Bomb resistance is explicitly disclaimed (§1.12); capping is the caller's job (§1.13). Contested vs KNOWN-NON-FINDING (§1.15 lists the recurring pattern) — the two closes overlap and the model flags this as an unratified-draft escalation point.

summary: Report that zlib-compressed data is fully readable because zlib performs no encryption of the payload.
requires: expectation that compression provides confidentiality
notes: Confidentiality/encryption is an explicit non-goal (§1.3/§1.12, FAQ:38). Compression is not a security transform.

summary: Sanitizer reports use of an uninitialized value inside deflate()'s matching loop.
requires: running deflate under MSan/Valgrind
notes: Documented recurring false positive: intentional for performance, output unaffected (§1.15, FAQ:36). Discharged by P5.

summary: Analyzer flags CRC-32 as a 'weak cryptographic hash' and recommends replacing it with SHA-256.
requires: policy scanner treating CRC-32 as a security hash
notes: Documented recurring false positive (§1.15): CRC is an error-detection code, not a MAC. Contested vs BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed (§1.12 false-friend) — the model lists both closes for this pattern.

summary: The official zlib release tarball on a download mirror was tampered with, differing from the signed source tree.
requires: attacker who controls a distribution mirror
notes: No §1.17 disposition covers distribution/supply-chain integrity; the model scopes only the source contract. Fits none cleanly → MODEL-GAP, triggering §1.16 to add an explicit scope exclusion. Contested: some route OUT-OF-MODEL by analogy.

summary: A memory-safety bug reported against the Linux kernel's forked zlib_inflate copy, filed as a 'zlib' vulnerability.
requires: the bug exists in a third-party fork, not madler/zlib HEAD
notes: The finding targets a different codebase (a downstream fork); no disposition covers 'not this project's code'. Fits none → MODEL-GAP, trigger §1.16. Contested vs OUT-OF-MODEL: unsupported-component by analogy.
